title: Weekly Usage and Shipment Spacing for a Second Pet on the Same Item under Tailwise Autoship
content:
**Household usage method — the new pet's share of an item**

(a) **Household usage.** The household's usage of the item is the units of the existing Autoship's scheduled shipments charged in the last six months, divided by 26 weeks.

(b) **What the existing Autoship covers.** The existing Autoship covers its own pet at its units per shipment divided by its weeks between shipments, per week.

(c) **The new pet's usage.** The new pet uses the household's usage less what the existing Autoship covers per week, and one unit lasts the new pet 7 divided by that weekly usage, in days.

(d) **Days between the new pet's shipments.** The units per shipment multiplied by the days one unit lasts the new pet, less the program's promised carrier transit days after the ship date.

(e) **Weeks.** Those days divided by 7, rounded down to a whole week, and never fewer than the program's shortest frequency nor more than its longest frequency.

A record counts as dated in the last six months when its date is later than the same calendar day six months before the day the value is worked out.

## Worked example (hypothetical; Autoship Everyday transit taken as 2 days and frequency range 1 to 26 weeks)

| Step | Figure |
|---|---|
| Scheduled-shipment units on the existing Autoship, last six months | 39 |
| Household usage: 39 divided by 26 | 1.5 units a week |
| Existing Autoship: 2 units every 4 weeks | 0.5 unit a week |
| New pet: 1.5 less 0.5 | 1.0 unit a week |
| One unit lasts: 7 divided by 1.0 | 7 days |
| Days: 2 units multiplied by 7, less 2 | 12 days |
| Weeks: 12 divided by 7, rounded down | 1 week |
